newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino Bre-X worker believes in Busang gold.
newsitem.headline: Filipino Bre-X worker believes in Busang gold.

text.p: A Filipino geologist for a Canadian firm linked to a huge mining scandal said on Tuesday he believed there was gold in the Busang property and doubted all the samples from the site could have been tampered with.

"Of course there is gold there...indications of gold," said Bob Ramirez, one of several Filipinos who worked at the now discredited gold property of Bre-X Minerals Ltd in the Indonesian jungles on the island of Borneo.
"There were so many samples. Could you have tampered with all of them?" he said on his return to Manila after the collapse of a project once touted as the world's greatest gold find this century.
Ramirez appeared with fellow Filipino Bre-X worker Manny Puspos at a news conference arranged by the Department of Foreign Affairs after their arrival from Jakarta.
Ramirez admitted, however, his work limited him only to the Busang exploration site and he was not in any way involved in the testing of samples.
Asked if the samples could have been tampered elsewhere, he said: "I am out of that already. I only worked at the site."
Ramirez spoke hesitantly, often only after repeated questioning by reporters. At times, he declined to answer. Puspos hardly spoke.
Bre-X became the darling of the mining world after it claimed its Busang gold property contained at least 70 million ounces of gold valued at about $25 billion at current prices.
The claim turned into stunning hoax after an independent audit firm found that the Busang data had been falsified on a scale unprecedented in mining history.
Ramirez, who said he worked at Busang for less than two years, told reporters he based his opinion that there was gold in Busang on "the surface exposure...the physical properties of the area.
"I am not saying there is a lot of gold there...but there are indications," he said.

Asked if he believed the gold samples taken from the site and tested elsewhere had been tampered with, he said: "No, sir. With so many drill holes, could there have been tampering?" Ramirez and Puspos said they knew nothing about the mysterious death of their chief Filipino geologist, Michael de Guzman, who fell from a helicopter while flying to Busang in March shortly before the hoax became publicly known.
"We don't know how he died," Ramirez said.
He declined to answer when asked about statements by Indonesian police that de Guzman committed suicide.
